theater: 奧龍特斯河谷與腓尼基海岸

battle.name: 第四次敘利亞戰役
battle.theater: 奧龍特斯河谷與腓尼基海岸
battle.brief: 前1466至前1454年，圖特摩斯三世第四次北征，聯軍首次由赫梯、米坦尼與塞浦路斯組成。埃及軍沒有能攻入對方本土，改以海陸封鎖切斷銅源與外援，最後以一紙和約收場，留下已知最早的國際和平條約。卡面埃及長矛是埃及步兵前排的制式兵器：矛牆頂住車兵衝撞，圍城時壓住城頭。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭是埃及新王國第十八王朝與一個橫跨安納托利亞、黎凡特與地中海東岸的聯軍聯盟之間的衝突，戰線從奧龍特斯河谷伸到腓尼基海岸，再外延到塞浦路斯。埃及一方以法老圖特摩斯三世（Menkheperre）為全軍最高統帥，國王自領近衛與王室弓手隊出戰；軍隊骨幹是步兵：前排為持長矛與大盾的重裝矛兵，中後排是數量最多的埃及弓手，備有角、筋、木製的複合弓與燙硬箭鏃，另有數百輛木輪雙輪戰車，御者與射手同車；隊伍中另有來自黎凡特、努比亞與西部沙漠的謝爾登人、麥傑人與沙漠部族充當傭兵與徵召兵，軍中文書記錄口糧配給與徵發物資。聯軍以赫梯王國為核心：舊王國崩解後散居高美索不達米亞的赫梯人重新建國，在安納托利亞高原恢復實力，其王以大王的名號向聯軍首領發號施令；米坦尼的胡里王國是聯盟支柱，國王同樣自稱大王，控制卡脫納、圖尼普、阿勒頗、比布魯斯與西頓一線的城邦，並在幼發拉底河中游的卡爾凱美什與埃馬爾扶植親信；塞浦路斯的阿爾夏伊亞王國站在聯軍一邊，握有地中海東岸最重要的銅礦與象牙來源。聯軍作戰以步兵、車兵與胡里弓手為骨幹，赫梯車兵的數量與質素最為突出。巴比倫此時仍與埃及平行通書，立場更接近仲裁者而非交戰方。
countriesEn: The war was a clash between Egypt of the Eighteenth Dynasty and a coalition league that stretched across Anatolia, the Levant and the eastern Mediterranean, with a front running from the valley of the Orontes to the Phoenician coast and out to Cyprus. On the Egyptian side the supreme commander was the pharaoh Thutmose III (Menkheperre), who led the host in person together with the royal guard and the royal corps of bowmen. The framework of the army was infantry: heavy spearmen with large shields in the front rank, and behind them the Egyptian archers, the largest contingent in the host, armed with composite bows of horn, sinew and wood and with fire-hardened arrowheads; there were also several hundred wooden two-wheeled chariots, driver and archer riding together. Sherden, Medjay and desert tribes from the Levant, Nubia and the western oases served as mercenaries and conscripts, and army scribes kept ration tallies and requisition lists. The core of the coalition was the Hittite kingdom: after the collapse of the old kingdom, the Hittites who had taken refuge in Upper Mesopotamia founded a new state and recovered their strength on the Anatolian plateau, and their king issued orders to the leader of the coalition in the name of the Great King. The Hurrian kingdom of Mitanni was the pillar of the alliance; its king likewise called himself the Great King, and he held the line of Qatna, Tunip, Aleppo, Byblos and Sidon, with clients of his own installed at Carchemish and Emar on the middle Euphrates. The kingdom of Alashiya on Cyprus stood with the coalition, holding the most important copper and ivory sources in the eastern Mediterranean. The coalition fought on infantry, chariots and Hurrian archers, and the Hittite chariot force was the most numerous and the most accomplished of the three. Babylonia still corresponded with Egypt on equal terms at this date and sat closer to the part of an arbiter than to that of a belligerent.
people: 這場戰役的核心人物是埃及法老圖特摩斯三世（Menkheperre），在位約三十八年，約前1479年至前1425年，生前發動過七至八次北征，本役是其中文獻最零落的一次。國王自任全軍統帥，日常指揮由宰相與弓箭手隊長一類的軍職分擔，軍中文書留下逐日行程與地名清單，後人才能循名單還原路線。他身後的繼承人阿蒙霍特普二世嗣位後不久即在敘利亞與赫梯的邊境重新動武，把本役勉強維持的均勢再度打破。對面的米坦尼大王在文獻中姓名不一，一般認為屬圖什拉塔一系，其繼任者圖什拉塔在阿瑪納字母中屢次向埃及索取黃金與銀兩，這批信件把本役的失敗寫成曠日持久的乞求。赫梯方面的締約君主姓名在學者之間仍有分歧，多作穆瓦塔里一世或穆爾西里二世，而赫梯舊王國的年代框架本身就有爭議，因此不宜斷定具體人選。塞浦路斯方面留下姓名的，是那位寫信給埃及法老、請求白銀並描述銅錠形狀與數量的阿爾夏伊亞王；這封信通常被繫於圖特摩斯三世時期，與本役同一時段，是已知最早的國際書信之一。學術史上還有兩批人決定了本役的樣貌：二十世紀的翻譯者先後破譯哈圖沙出土的楔形文條約泥板，確認締約者為圖特摩斯三世；2010年考古團隊在哈圖沙再發現一份楔形文副本，又為這場戰爭添了一紙硬證。
peopleEn: The central figure is the Egyptian pharaoh Thutmose III (Menkheperre), who reigned about thirty-eight years, roughly from 1479 to 1425 BC, and who launched seven or eight northern campaigns in his lifetime; this war is the least documented of them. The king was his own commander-in-chief, with day-to-day control delegated to the vizier and to offices such as the chief of the bowmen, while army scribes drew up day-by-day itineraries and lists of place names, and it is from those lists that the route can be reconstructed at all. His successor Amenhotep II renewed the war on the Syrian and Hittite frontier shortly after his accession, breaking the even balance that this campaign had barely maintained. On the other side the Great King of Mitanni is named differently in different documents and is generally placed in the line of Tushratta, whose successor, Tushratta himself, asked Egypt for gold and silver again and again in the Amarna letters, turning the defeat of this war into a long-running petition. The name of the Hittite signatory is still disputed among scholars, who take him to be either Muwatalli I or Mursili II, and since the chronology of the Hittite old kingdom is itself contested, no firm identification should be made. From the Cypriot side the name that survives belongs to the king of Alashiya who wrote to the Egyptian pharaoh asking for silver and describing the shape and quantity of his copper ingots; the letter is usually assigned to the reign of Thutmose III and to the same stretch of time as this war, and it is among the oldest surviving international letters. Two further groups of men shaped how this war looks to us: the translators of the twentieth century who read the cuneiform treaty tablets excavated at Hattusa and identified the pharaoh as Thutmose III, and the archaeological team that in 2010 uncovered a further cuneiform copy at the same site, adding one more hard document to the case.
kits: 本卡兵器是埃及長矛。早王朝已出現的制式長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，矛尖能刺穿軟甲與皮甲，也能在被格擋時承受反作用力；到第十八王朝，形制已改為更細長的菱形有脊矛頭，帶套筒，杆身以皮條或麻繩纏紮加固，卡面所繪的早王朝形制與本役相隔近一千七百年，但兵器在體系裡的位置一路未變：它是埃及步兵前排最普遍、最廉價的近戰兵器，也是邊防堡壘與城垣守備的標準武備。守城要的不是砍劈，而是把來犯者擋在台階之下，長矛正好。落到這場戰役的具體場景：會戰中，前排矛手在弓兵箭雨之後接住聯軍步兵與車兵，矛牆把失去衝力的散兵頂回去；圍城時，埃及人把長矛架在斜坡與雲梯旁，對準城頭與正在爬梯的人；守備線上，長矛是堡壘日常的值班武備。埃及步兵整體裝備還包括月牙形青銅短劍、長柄銅斧與短匕，弓手是軍隊中數量最多的一環；車兵是突破與追擊的力量，木輪雙輪車，四馬挽的車漸多。攻城方面備有攻城塔、撞錘、填土斜坡與投石索，弓手與標槍先壓制城頭。聯軍方面，赫梯車兵擅長單馬與雙馬輕車，適合黎凡特山區的機動；胡里與敘利亞弓手同用複合弓，近戰則以銅斧為主；塞浦路斯與腓尼基的船隻負責把銅料與援軍送上地中海。補給靠驢騾隊與牛車運糧，以及城邦徵發的穀物、葡萄酒與金屬；銅來自西奈與塞浦路斯，錫與青金石經巴比倫方向運來。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the Egyptian spear. The standard long spear already existed in the Early Dynastic period, with a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, a point able to pierce soft and leather armour and able to take the recoil of a blow that was parried; by the Eighteenth Dynasty the form had changed into a longer, rhomboid, midribbed head with a socket, the shaft reinforced by thongs or cord wrappings. The form drawn on the card belongs to a period some seventeen hundred years before this war, but the weapon's place in the order of battle never changed: it was the most universal and cheapest close-combat arm of the Egyptian infantry in the front rank, and the standard arm of frontier fortresses and city walls, because what a siege needs is not chopping but the means of holding attackers below the steps, and that is precisely what a spear is. In this war the card's weapon has two concrete settings. In pitched battle the spearmen in the leading files met the coalition infantry and chariots after the archers' arrow-fall, and the wall of spear-points pushed back troops whose momentum had already been broken. In the siege the Egyptians planted their spears along the ramp and beside the ladders, aimed at the wall and at the men coming up them; on the line of defence the spear was the standing weapon of the garrison. The rest of the Egyptian loadout included the inward-curving bronze khopesh, long-handled bronze axes and short daggers, and the archers were the largest single contingent in the army. Chariotry was the force for breakthrough and pursuit: wooden two-wheeled cars, with four-horse teams becoming commoner. For siege work the Egyptians had towers, battering rams, earth ramps and slings, clearing the wall with arrows and javelins first. On the coalition side the Hittite charioteers were skilled with the light single-horse and two-horse cars that suited movement in the Syrian hills; Hurrian and Syrian archers used composite bows as well, and close combat turned on the bronze axe; the ships of Cyprus and Phoenicia carried copper and reinforcements across the Mediterranean. Supply came up with donkey and mule trains and ox carts carrying grain, together with the requisitioned grain, wine and metal of the city-states; the copper came from Sinai and Cyprus, and tin and lapis lazuli arrived by way of Babylon.
tactics: 第四次的打法與前幾次不同，重心由會戰轉為封鎖。埃及軍沒有硬推幼發拉底河，而是沿腓尼基海岸與塞浦路斯之間切聯軍的補給：船隊封鎖港口，船隻由尼羅河經運河入海，再沿海路北上，必要時甚至把船拖過陸地作搬運，運載車兵與糧食登陸；陸軍則在黎凡特平原與黎巴嫩山脈西麓之間進退，努力切斷阿爾夏伊亞通往西頓、比布魯斯的銅料通道。會戰時，埃及的慣例是弓兵在兩翼展開成弧形，以連續箭幕削弱敵軍前排，車兵不置於前線，留待敵陣出現缺口才一齊投入衝開缺口，然後步兵帶著長矛與月牙劍湧入作近身格鬥；前排矛手相互搭著肩背，把前列變成一堵推不倒的牆，矛的長度正好頂住失去衝力的散兵。聯軍的赫梯車兵善於利用山道與沙丘地帶襲擊縱隊側翼，迫使埃及把縱隊收成密陣，盾與盾相接，弓手退到矛牆後方還射。圍城多以圍而不打與突擊並用：先以投石索、弓手與標槍清理城頭，再以雲梯攀城或斷糧迫降，必要時堆土築斜坡，把車兵送上城牆高度；守方的胡里弓手從城頭反覆射擊，攻城一方就得在盾牆下把雲梯一次次扶正。遠征有嚴格的季節：一般於春末四五月出發，沿途宿營於水泉充足的城郊或廢墟，冬季地中海沿岸多雨、道路泥濘、車兵難行，軍隊便停止攻勢，翌年再戰；正是在這種年年拉鋸的節奏裡，雙方從戰場轉到談判桌。
tacticsEn: The conduct of the fourth campaign differed from its predecessors: the centre of gravity shifted from pitched battle to blockade. The Egyptian army did not push hard at the Euphrates, but cut the coalition's supply between the Phoenician coast and Cyprus. A squadron of ships closed the harbours, the vessels passing from the Nile into the sea by canal and then working north along the coast, and at times the ships were even dragged overland by portage so that they could carry chariots and grain ashore. The land army worked in and out between the plains of the Levant and the western slopes of Mount Lebanon, trying to cut the copper road that ran from Alashiya to Sidon and Byblos. In pitched battle the Egyptian habit was to deploy the archers in a crescent on the wings, wearing down the enemy front with a continuous curtain of arrows, while the chariots were not committed to the front but were launched together when a gap opened, and only then did the infantry with their spears and their khopesh pour through and finish the business at close quarters. The spearmen in the leading files overlapped their shields and shoulders so that the front became a wall that could not easily be pushed aside, and the reach of their spears was exactly the reach needed against troops whose momentum had been broken. The Hittite chariots were good at using the tracks and dune country to strike the flanks of the marching columns, which forced Egypt to close up into a dense formation with shield against shield while the archers fell back behind the spear wall and shot over it. Sieges combined blockade with sudden assault: the wall was first cleared with slings, arrows and javelins, then scaled with ladders or reduced by starvation, and where necessary earth was tipped up into a ramp to bring the chariots to the height of the rampart; the Hurrian archers on the wall shot back repeatedly, so the besiegers had to set the ladders upright again and again under cover of their shield wall. The campaign followed a strict seasonal rhythm: the army generally set out in late spring, in the fourth and fifth months of the year, and camped on the outskirts of towns and among ruins wherever springs and cisterns gave water; in the winter the Mediterranean coast was wet with rain, the roads turned to mud and chariots could hardly move, so the army simply stopped attacking and the war was resumed the following year. It was out of that year-by-year rhythm of attrition that the two sides moved from the battlefield to the negotiating table.
data: 可核對的數字如下。年代通常記作前1466年至前1454年之間，也有學者放在前1460年代中段至前1450年代初；和約一般定在前1454年前後。圖特摩斯三世在位約三十八年，約前1479年至前1425年，前後發動七至八次北征。距離方面，底比斯至阿勒頗直線約一千三百公里，至塞浦路斯東岸約一千一百公里；由尼羅河三角洲到塞浦路斯東岸的航程約六百公里；以每日二十五至三十公里的行軍速度計，單程遠征就要數十日。兵力方面，埃及核心步兵一般估計在數千至一萬之間，其中弓手占多數，車兵常在數百輛的量級，部分估算高至逾千輛；聯軍靠各城邦與赫梯、米坦尼拼湊，總數相若，但車兵比例明顯高於埃及，組織也更鬆散。條約文本方面，現存象形文石碑一件，楔形字泥板數件出自赫梯首都哈圖沙，2010年在同一地點另發現一份楔形文副本。條約內文寫明雙方各贈對方一千塊白銀，是互惠的友誼之禮而非納貢。此外，阿爾夏伊亞書信描述了銅錠的形狀與成批的數量，說明塞浦路斯的銅是經談判分配而非自由交易。埃及碑文常以擄獲人數、馬匹與金銀器計功，數量多被後世學者調低數倍，宜視為宣傳量度而非統計。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked run as follows. The date is normally given as between 1466 and 1454 BC, though some scholars place it in the middle of the 1460s to the early 1450s; the peace treaty is generally dated to around 1454 BC. Thutmose III reigned about thirty-eight years, roughly from 1479 to 1425 BC, and made seven or eight northern campaigns. As for distances: the straight line from Thebes to Aleppo is about thirteen hundred kilometres, and to the east coast of Cyprus about eleven hundred; the sea run from the Nile Delta to the east coast of Cyprus is about six hundred kilometres; at a marching rate of twenty-five to thirty kilometres a day, the outward march alone took weeks. On numbers of men: the Egyptian core infantry is generally estimated at several thousand up to ten thousand, with archers forming the majority of it, and chariots usually counted in the hundreds, though some estimates run past a thousand; the coalition was assembled from the city-states together with the Hittites and Mitanni and came to a comparable total, but with a markedly higher proportion of chariots and a looser organisation. As for the treaty texts: one hieroglyphic stele survives, together with a number of cuneiform tablets from the Hittite capital of Hattusa, and in 2010 a further cuneiform copy was uncovered at the same site. The text records that each side gives the other a thousand pieces of silver, a reciprocal token of friendship rather than tribute. In addition, the Alashiya letter describes the shape of the copper ingots and the number of them in a consignment, which shows that the Cypriot copper was distributed by agreement rather than by free trade. Egyptian monuments habitually score their victories in prisoners, horses and plate, and those numbers have routinely been cut by later scholars by a factor of several, so they are better read as propaganda measures than as statistics.
cause: 打起來的原因有三層。最外層是地理與商路：埃及要保住從西奈與塞浦路斯運出的銅礦、從黎巴嫩運入的雪松木，以及經米坦尼轉手自巴比倫方向流入的青金石，這條商路一旦被截斷，新王國的財政與神廟工程都要停滯。中層是邊界與宗主權之爭：赫梯人在安納托利亞重建的國家急欲伸入北敘利亞，而米坦尼大王在西屬的城邦面前自居宗主，埃及則要否認這層宗主關係，寧可自己收編卡脫納、圖尼普與阿勒頗；塞浦路斯站在聯軍一邊，等於掐住埃及銅料的另一條來源。最內層是政治與時機：圖特摩斯三世成年後需要北方戰功來鞏固王位與一批有戰功的將領，赫梯與米坦尼之間的矛盾又給了他插手北方的理由；而前幾次遠征雖把戰線推上去，卻始終沒有取得北岸的實際控制，聯盟趁機收緊對埃及商隊與城邦的約束，兩國關係被推向攤牌。於是法老再度自南敘利亞出發，這回的目標不是某一座邊境小城，而是整條北界與聯盟的團結。
causeEn: The war began for three layers of reason. The outermost was geography and trade: Egypt had to keep the copper coming down from Sinai and Cyprus, the cedar coming in from the Levant, and the lapis lazuli arriving through Mitanni from the Babylonian direction, and if that route were cut the finances and the temple works of the New Kingdom would all stall. The middle layer was a quarrel over the frontier and over overlordship: the Hittite state rebuilt in Anatolia was eager to reach into northern Syria, while the Great King of Mitanni claimed the city-states there as his own subordinates, and Egypt denied him that claim, preferring to take Qatna, Tunip and Aleppo into its own hand; Cyprus standing with the coalition meant choking the other source of Egyptian copper. The innermost layer was political and opportunistic: once grown, Thutmose III needed northern victories to shore up his throne and to reward a circle of commanders, and the quarrel between the Hittites and Mitanni gave him a pretext to interfere in the north; and while the earlier campaigns had pushed the line forward, they had never gained effective control of the far bank, so the league used the opportunity to tighten its grip on Egyptian caravans and city-states and pushed the two courts towards a showdown. The pharaoh therefore set out from southern Syria once more, and this time the mark was not a single frontier town but the whole northern frontier and the cohesion of the league.
impact: 對埃及，這場戰役的結果是一條以條約固定下來的邊界，以及黎凡特宗主體系的延續：卡脫納、圖尼普、比布魯斯、西頓與阿勒頗繼續進貢金、銀、鉛、錫、銅、象牙、馬匹、葡萄酒與人丁，塞浦路斯的銅料也以協議方式穩定流向埃及。更大的影響在外交形式上：這份雙方互贈白銀、劃定界線、互不侵犯、遇襲須援助、逃亡者應予遣返的文本，被後世視為已知最早的國際和平條約，它示範了以條約代替佔領來管理邊界的方式，亞述、新巴比倫與後來埃及赫梯之間的卡迭什和約，都在不同程度上沿用這套辦法。對赫梯與米坦尼，這是一場體面而實際的撤退：赫梯承認既有邊界，聯盟解散，米坦尼在敘利亞的樞紐地位喪失，兩國的角力延後到阿蒙霍特普四世時期才因埃及其他政策而短暫中斷，又於前13世紀由拉美西斯二世與穆瓦塔里二世在卡爾凱美什的大戰重新爆發。學術上，這份條約是重建阿瑪納時代國際關係的關鍵材料，兩種文字版本的分歧還揭示出埃及觀念裡國界與主權的不同算法。
impactEn: For Egypt the war produced a frontier fixed in a treaty and the continuation of the Levantine system of overlordship: Qatna, Tunip, Byblos, Sidon and Aleppo went on paying tribute in gold, silver, lead, tin, copper, ivory, horses, wine and labour, and Cypriot copper now flowed to Egypt by agreement. The larger effect was on the form of diplomacy: this text, in which each side gives the other silver, the border is drawn, neither invades the other, each is to aid the other if attacked, and runaways are to be returned, is regarded as the earliest known international peace treaty. It demonstrated the management of frontiers by treaty rather than by occupation, and the later arrangements of Assyria, of Babylonia, and of the Egyptian-Hittite peace of Kadesh all followed that method in some degree. For the Hittites and Mitanni this was an honourable and real retreat: the Hittites accepted the existing border, the league came apart, and Mitanni lost its pivot position in Syria; the rivalry between the two powers was deferred until the reign of Amenhotep IV interrupted it briefly for other reasons, and broke out again in the thirteenth century in the great battle between Ramses II and Muwatalli II at Carchemish. In scholarship the treaty is a key document for reconstructing the international order of the Amarna age, and the differences between the two language versions even reveal the different Egyptian notions of border and sovereignty.
result: 結果是戰爭以和約收束，而非以戰場勝負定案。聯軍在野戰中沒有崩潰，卻失去了協同：赫梯退回安納托利亞並接受既有邊界，米坦尼的城邦網被埃及逐個收編，塞浦路斯轉向與埃及協議，銅料來源重新打開。前1454年前後，埃及與赫梯簽下雙邊條約，寫明互不侵犯、劃定疆界、對方遭攻擊時不予援助、逃亡者遣返，並各贈對方一千塊白銀；文本有象形文與楔形字兩種版本，象形文石碑今藏於紐約聯合國，楔形字泥板出自哈圖沙，2010年另發現的副本為研究提供了新的一件。埃及在這一役的實際收穫是保住商路、銅源與宗主權的框架，未能迫使赫梯承認其對敘利亞的主權；所謂第四次敘利亞戰役，在圖特摩斯三世的系列戰爭中屬少數沒有大戰的役次，之後的戰線略有退卻，直到第六役才重新拉直。史料有限，戰役過程多靠卡爾納克年表殘片、軍隊地名表與條約文本拼回：矛手在前列頂住車兵、封鎖船隊切斷銅源、冬季停戰與翌年再戰的循環，是這場戰爭留給後世最清楚的畫面。
resultEn: The outcome was that the war was wound up by a treaty rather than decided on the field. The coalition did not collapse in battle but lost its cohesion: the Hittites withdrew to Anatolia and accepted the existing border, the network of Mitanni city-states was picked off one by one into the Egyptian sphere, Cyprus turned to an agreement with Egypt, and the copper supply was reopened. Around 1454 BC Egypt and the Hittites signed a bilateral treaty stipulating mutual non-aggression, a defined frontier, no aid to the other in the event of attack, and the return of runaways, each side giving the other a thousand pieces of silver. The text exists in hieroglyphic and cuneiform versions: the hieroglyphic stele is kept in New York at the United Nations, the cuneiform tablets come from Hattusa, and the copy found in 2010 gave the study one more document. Egypt's practical gains in this campaign were the trade routes, the copper and the framework of its overlordship; it did not force the Hittites to acknowledge Egyptian sovereignty over Syria. As the fourth of the Syrian wars it counts among the few of Thutmose III's campaigns that contained no great battle, and the line of contact gave a little ground afterwards until the sixth campaign straightened it once more. The evidence is thin, and the course of the war has to be pieced together from the fragments of the Karnak annals, the army's topographical list and the treaty text: the spearmen holding the front against the chariots, the squadrons cutting off the copper by sea, the winter stand and the campaign resumed in the spring, these are the clearest pictures the war has left behind.
